# HCC · Celestial Atlas

> A single-page atlas of physics laboratories that COMPUTE. Opening the page
> gives an agent a live numerical instrument, not a document about one. Every
> number below was produced by running the thing that produced it.

This file exists because the capability was already here and nothing announced
it. An agent that knew to call `HCC_API` got real physics; an agent that merely
opened the URL was told nothing. That was measured, and this is the fix.

## Scientific workspace and static SDK

Start with `api/agent.json`. All resource paths in that descriptor resolve from the Atlas site root.
Human workspace: `agent.html`. No account or GPU is required.

- `api/agent-client.mjs`: ESM SDK, `connectAtlas(baseURL)` -> discover, search, describe, forecast, audit.
- `api/forecast-audit.schema.json`: complete input format for chronological forecast scoring.
- `atlas.audit(input)` returns MAE, RMSE, signed bias, baseline MSE skill, interval coverage and interval score, exact horizon groups, supplied provenance and replayable SHA-256 input.
- `forecast(control, delta)` returns a conditional scaling scenario, NOT a calibrated empirical prediction. Null evidence stays null. Perturbation endpoints are not confidence intervals.
- Observational labels and issue timestamps are caller declarations. Synthetic examples remain SYNTHETIC_ONLY; no automatic empirical validation is claimed.
- Fetch-only agents can inspect all JSON contracts. Browser agents can import the SDK by URL. Node 18+ agents should download the source and import the local module; Node does not import HTTPS modules by default.
- Public GitHub Pages hosts static resources, NOT the POST /mcp or /api/v1 compute endpoints. For those, run `node server/server.mjs`; default origin is http://127.0.0.1:8974. The same audit is registered as `prediction.holdout_audit`.
- The SDK does not modify the public site or grant publication credentials. Local computations need no secret credentials.

## Full Atlas runtime

Load the page and wait for the runtime:

    await HCC_API.ready({ timeout: 20000 })

Then compute. This is a real call and a real answer:

    HCC_API.evaluate('bb', { T: 5772 })
    → { radiance: 2.6239e13,
        lambda_max: 5.0204e-7,      // 502 nm — the solar peak, from Wien
        exitance: 6.2939e7,          // W/m² — from Stefan–Boltzmann
        peak_radiance: 2.6240e13,
        fraction_of_peak: 0.99996 }

Add `?render=0` to the URL to skip WebGL entirely. The physics does not need it,
and `HCC_API.capabilities()` will tell you what the browser gave you.

## The surface

    version  ready  schema  help  health  capabilities
    list     describe  evaluate        laboratories, their contracts, their answers — counts in api/manifest.json
    bus      links  wires  publishes   what is coupled to what
    bus.refusal  bus.refusals          WHY a coupling was refused, in writing
    bus.contested  bus.isolated  bus.counterfactual
    unmeasured                          what this atlas admits it has not measured
    reach  sensitivity  transfers  liveness
    stations                            sub-stations of a laboratory: .of .all .current .go
    scales  siUnits  instruments  selftest  report  markdown  ui

And beside it, the same contracts read four more ways:

    HCC_PSPACE.open(id)            any output over any two inputs as a surface; the power law
                                   it obeys (exponents as fractions); the Jacobian at a point;
                                   a phase portrait along a clock; bus doors that carry values
    HCC_INVARIANTS.find(id,along)  which combinations of the outputs never move — across the
                                   domain, or along one input (a clock: conserved quantities)
    HCC_INVARIANTS.symmetries(id)  scalings x → λ^k x that move nothing, applied before believed
    HCC_INVARIANTS.across(a,b)     laws across one bus link that neither laboratory states alone
    HCC_FEEDS                      the Sun, planets, named stars, galaxies, quasars — measured
                                   numbers, with provenance, fed into laboratory inputs
    HCC_STATS                      the classical statistics of the atlas's own catalogues

`describe(id)` returns a typed contract: inputs with units and domains, outputs,
the verifiers that guard it, and its prediction class — exact, numerical,
reference, conditional or exploratory. A laboratory never claims more than its
class allows.

## What is unusual here

**Refusals are first-class.** `bus.refusals` returns couplings the atlas declined
and the reason for each. A quantity bus that only reported what connects would be
half an instrument.

**Coincidences are tested for being coincidences.** Where two independently
computed numbers agree, the atlas varies a parameter neither side declares and
reports whether the agreement survives. Some do not, and it says so.

**Invariants are found, not declared.** Every laboratory is asked the same question —
which combinations of its outputs never move — by one finder that samples it through its
contract, keeps only minimal exact relations, names constants in closed form only to
1e-10, and applies every symmetry at random points before reporting it. The census is in
`api/invariants.json`: laws inside laboratories, and laws across the bus that no single
laboratory states (a Jeans mass carried into Hawking's law keeps M·T_H = ħc³/(8πG k_B)).

**Laws are found from the inputs.** The same census also asks what each output IS as a
function of the inputs that moved: a power law over every positive input at once, else the
smallest sum of at most three library terms plus a constant, for the output and — where that
is not exact — its square and reciprocal. It returns the f-sum rule π/2·ω_p², the multiplicity
2l + 1, a spinor's half angle cos(θ/2), σ_SB·T⁴ and M² = 1 + ZT from the laboratories
themselves (`laws` per laboratory in `api/invariants.json`).

**A field is drawn as its shape.** The Field Lab's default view is the geometry of the
field it integrates: level sets by marching tetrahedra (watertight, area and enclosed volume
measured), lines of −∇u from every source, a slice with isolines, |ψ|² coloured by the phase
of ψ, and for the 3D Ising lattice its exact domain walls — one dual plaquette per
antiparallel bond, whose area is the energy, E/N³ = −3 + 2W/N³. `HCC_FIELD.open(model,
preset)` and `HCC_FIELD.structure()` drive and read it.
Three laws are then read off the drawing: Gauss's law on every equipotential (Φ/Q → 1 once
`HCC_FIELD.converge()` has relaxed Poisson by SOR), the widest moment of a fixed isotherm of a
diffusing pulse (r² = ⟨r²⟩ exactly, whatever D, level or width), and the 3D Ising critical point
from crossing Binder cumulants with Wolff clusters (`HCC_FIELD.critical()`, T_c ≈ 4.51 J/k_B).

**A map of the Universe, at every level.** After Ménard & Shtarkman: the observer at the bottom,
the first light at the top, every object the atlas holds at its true distance — planets, 15 230
Hipparcos stars with a parallax, the Milky Way's nebulae, 4 341 galaxies, 5 959 quasars, and the
CMB at z = 1090 (13.86 Gpc comoving, radiation included). Linear, as in the original: everything
with a name sits in the bottom 2.4 %, quasars reach 55 %. Logarithmic: one strip, sixteen
decades, every level. The SDSS band the original fills is drawn as a labelled gap; the CMB band is
a Gaussian realisation, not the Planck map. `HCC_UMAP.open()`, `HCC_UMAP.stats()`.

**∃! The only possible laws.** `api/uniqueness.json` (from `scripts/uniqueness.mjs`): for each of
the 185 exact power laws, the smallest set of constants from {G, c, ħ, k_B, m_e, m_p} that makes it
consistent, and Buckingham's count of dimensionless groups. 48 are forced — the only formula units
allow — and 43 have their pure number named: π²/60 (Stefan–Boltzmann, forced by c, ħ, k_B), 2π/x_W
(Wien), π²/45 (radiation pressure), √(2π) (thermal wavelength), (3π²)^{2/3}/2 (Fermi),
2π/ζ(3/2)^{2/3} (BEC), π·e^−γ and e^γ/π² (BCS), π²/240 (Casimir), 3/5 (a uniform sphere),
π²/8 (the Local Group's timing mass), ln 2 (Landauer). 86 are free: their form is physics —
Bekenstein–Hawking's S = A/4 among them.

**Open problems are published.** `/api/v1/open-problems` and `api/open-problems.json`
carry what this atlas knows it has not done, including defects found in its own
verifiers.

## Static, no browser required

    api/manifest.json        every laboratory, instrument and contract
    api/openapi.json         12 REST paths
    .well-known/mcp.json     9 MCP tools — list_labs, run_lab, sweep_lab, …
    api/sensitivity.json     every declared input swept, log-log slope fitted
    api/transfers.json       what actually moves along each coupling
    api/reach.json           what a control can reach, and how deep
    api/liveness.json        which views recompute per frame
    api/invariants.json      what every laboratory keeps, the law of each output, its symmetries, the laws across the bus
    api/open-problems.json   the unfinished list
    version.json             release identity

## Ground rules

Read `SCIENTIFIC_CONTRACT.md` before quoting a number as a prediction. The short
form: a value carries the class of the model that produced it, and an exact model
consequence is not an empirical forecast.
